channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: A Q&A with Mads Magnussen
item.description: The Norwegian Competition Authority is likely to use its new competition tool this year, with the digital sector among several markets under consideration, the agency’s new director general has said. Former Wikborg Rein partner Mads Magnussen spoke to GCR about his ambition to close low-impact cases more quickly and improve engagement with parties under investigation.

item.title: Canadian draft merger guidelines sideline efficiencies, interest groups warn
item.description: Canada’s draft merger enforcement guidelines fail to properly account for efficiencies arguments and reduce the importance of procompetitive benefits to a “secondary consideration”, advocacy groups with links to major digital platforms have told the Competition Bureau.

item.title: Hamer: Expect greater Tunney Act scrutiny
item.description: Judicial scrutiny of Department of Justice settlements will be “greater than ever”, former deputy assistant attorney general Mark Hamer has said, downplaying the effectiveness of lobbying cases to the White House and cabinet members.

item.title: The pain train: The Tipline for 13 February 2026
item.description: The Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern merger is poised to hurt shippers, energy companies and American competitiveness, according to a group of Republican state enforcers. The deal would facilitate consolidation and raise prices in a manner “fundamentally at odds with an America-First economy”, the states told the Department of Justice on Thursday. item.title: Antitrust bar uncertain of HSR appeal
item.description: The Trump Administration’s support for an overhauled merger filing process does not guarantee it would appeal against a decision overturning the new Hart-Scott-Rodino Act form, several antitrust practitioners have said.

item.title: Assefi elevates leadership team
item.description: The acting head of the Department of Justice’s antitrust division has tapped a new team of litigators to fill the front office following a host of senior departures.

item.title: Slater: “I was just doing my job”
item.description: The former head of the Department of Justice’s antitrust division has hit back at the “smears” which circulated her shock exit in an exclusive interview with GCR.

item.title: Still got wings: The Briefing for 16 February 2026
item.description: Red Bull has not exhausted its energy for challenging EU dawn raids on its premises, asking the European Court of Justice to set aside a lower court ruling that upheld an inspection decision last year. The company claims the EU General Court committed errors of law and procedure in appeal grounds published today. item.title: Senate democrats urge CFIUS probe into UAE–backed crypto acquisition
item.description: A United Arab Emirates-backed fund’s reported $500 million acquisition of a stake in the Trump family’s cryptocurrency business raises “significant” national security concerns over access to sensitive data, two democratic party senators have told the US Treasury Secretary.

item.title: EU closes abuse probe into Edwards Lifesciences
item.description: Edwards Lifesciences has escaped an EU abuse of dominance probe by removing an "anti-copycatting" policy after the European Commission raised concerns that it could foreclose a rival.
